identity.name: PARK MEDI WORLD LIMITED
identity.industry: Affordable Private Hospital Chains / North India Cluster

summary.oneLiner: Second largest private hospital chain in North India and the largest in Haryana by bed capacity, operating 14 NABH-accredited multi-super-specialty hospitals under the 'Park' brand.
summary.business: Park Medi World operates a network of 14 NABH-accredited multi-super-specialty hospitals across Haryana, New Delhi, Punjab and Rajasthan under the 'Park' brand, offering over 30 super-specialty and specialty services. It serves largely lower-middle and middle-class patients, with revenue heavily weighted to government schemes/PSUs, and has grown through a cluster-based mix of organic build-out and hospital acquisitions.

currentContext.business: Park Medi World operates a network of 14 NABH-accredited multi-super-specialty hospitals across Haryana, New Delhi, Punjab and Rajasthan under the 'Park' brand, offering over 30 super-specialty and specialty services. It serves largely lower-middle and middle-class patients, with revenue heavily weighted to government schemes/PSUs, and has grown through a cluster-based mix of organic build-out and hospital acquisitions.
currentContext.expansion: Bed capacity grew from 2,550 (Mar 2023) to 3,250 (Sep 2025); pipeline in Ambala, Panchkula, Rohtak, New Delhi, Gorakhpur and Kanpur. Ambala expanding from 250 to 450 beds plus onco-radiation (operational by Oct 2027); Panchkula 300-bed hospital (by Apr 2026); Rohtak 250-bed hospital (by Dec 2026); Gorakhpur 400-bed O&M hospital (by Apr 2026); Kanpur 300-bed hospital under renovation (by Apr 2026). Company expects total bed capacity to rise to 4,900 beds by March 31, 2028.

one-line thesis: Park Medi World delivered record FY26 performance with 21% revenue growth and 26% EBITDA margins, driven by a 20% bed capacity addition and operational leverage, while positioning itself as the primary beneficiary of the 12-15% CGHS rate hike expected to flow through in FY27. The company's debt-free balance sheet and rapid integration of distressed assets (Bathinda, Agra) validate a capital-efficient expansion model targeting 5,460 beds by FY28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 460cr (Q4, +30% YoY), INR 1,679cr (FY26, +21% YoY); EBITDA: INR 127cr (Q4, +44% YoY, 28% margin), INR 444cr (FY26, +20% YoY, 26% margin); PAT: INR 77cr (Q4, +47% YoY), INR 274cr (FY26, +27% YoY); Order Book: N/A (Service sector); Net Debt: Negligible (Gross term loan INR 28cr vs Cash/FDs INR 352cr); One-offs: Accounting reclassification of Bathinda unit from standalone to subsidiary caused QoQ standalone revenue drop, no consolidated impact.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 7-7.5% appreciation in FY27 from CGHS hike (9-month impact); Margins: Expected to hold/expand despite Greenfield ramp (Panchkula) due to CGHS benefits and high occupancy in new Brownfield units; Order Inflow: Occupancy ramping at 65-70% for Bathinda, INR 5cr/month run-rate for Agra; Capex: INR 500cr planned over next 2 years for 1,500 new beds.
order book & pipeline: 1,500 beds under execution (Panchkula commissioned, Mohali expansion, Rohtak, Kanpur, Gorakhpur planned); Target capacity 5,460 beds by March 2028.
segment / subsidiary detail: High-end specialties (Cardio, Onco, Neuro, Ortho) now 56.9% of revenue (+316 bps YoY); Oncology revenue share grew to 6.5% (FY26) from 5% (FY25); 150+ kidney transplants, 4,700+ PTCA, 2,600+ robotic joint replacements performed in FY26.
growth verticals / optionality: Uttar Pradesh expansion (0 to 1,060 beds by FY28 via Agra, Kanpur, Gorakhpur clusters); Tri-City dominance with Panchkula + Mohali expansion (850 beds); Ambala oncology extension; Potential for further distressed asset acquisitions in North India.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 margin expansion (268 bps) driven by high occupancy and operating leverage in existing units; Greenfield units (Panchkula) expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in 12-15 months; Brownfield units (Bathinda, Agra) achieved PAT positivity within first month/year; Vendor negotiations mitigated oncology drug cost pressures.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex & Acquisitions: INR 430cr (Panchkula Greenfield INR 125cr for 350 beds ~INR 35L/bed, Bathinda, Agra, Narela acquisition); Future Capex: INR 500cr over 2 years for 1,500 beds.
capital allocation: Debt repayment priority (INR 28cr outstanding to be cleared); Organic growth (Greenfield/Brownfield); Opportunistic acquisitions of distressed assets; No dividend mentioned, focus on reinvestment for capacity doubling.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on rapid capacity addition (1,500 beds in 2 years); Regulatory changes in CGHS/insurance rates beyond current hike; Talent acquisition for new units; Integration risks in acquired distressed assets.
management quality / tone: Highly confident; Emphasis on 'capital efficiency', 'affordable healthcare', and 'operational discipline'; Transparent on CGHS benefits and receivable improvements (Debtor days down to 129 from 161).
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly reframes ARPOB analysis, arguing expenses should be benchmarked to total revenue per bed-count rather than ARPOB alone, highlighting their high-volume/low-cost model vs. premium competitors; Bathinda unit turned PAT positive in month one of acquisition, defying typical turnaround timelines.

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
